svg.title: CloudFront routes WordPress requests to two origins
svg.desc: Route 53 DNS maps the website hostname to CloudFront. Users send web requests directly to CloudFront. This example stores public media matching wp-content/uploads/* in a private S3 bucket; Origin Access Control signs requests to the bucket endpoint. Other requests go through a CloudFront VPC origin to an internal Application Load Balancer and WordPress EC2 instances in private subnets. Media responses can be cached; login and administration responses are not cached. A cache hit returns a reusable cached response from CloudFront, avoiding origin retrieval.
svg.text: CloudFront routes WordPress requests to two origins
Public media in a private S3 bucket; application servers in private subnets.
Cache hit: reuse a cached response. Origin arrows apply when an origin response is needed.
